'''James Eric Dahlberg''' is an emeritus professor of biomolecular chemistry at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].<ref name="morgridge1">{{cite web|url=https://morgridge.org/story/james-dahlberg-scientific-successes-enhanced-by-chance/|title=James Dahlberg: Scientific successes enhanced by chance|publisher=Morgridge Institute for Research|date=June 15, 2014|accessdate=May 13, 2020}}</ref> His research focuses on the biology of [[RNA]]. He was elected to the United States [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1996.

==Education==
Dahlberg earned his bachelor's degree from [[Haverford College]] in 1962 and his Ph.D. from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1966.<ref name="facweb">{{cite web|url=https://bmolchem.wisc.edu/staff/dahlberg-james/|title=JAMES DAHLBERG PROFESSOR EMERITUS|date=5 July 2017 |publisher=University of Wisconsin|accessdate=May 13, 2020}}</ref> He completed his postdoctoral training at the [[MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] in Cambridge with [[Frederick Sanger]] from 1966 to 1968 followed by additional work at the [[University of Geneva]] from 1968 to 1969.

==Career==
Dahlberg joined the faculty at the University of Wisconsin Department of Physiological Chemistry, which eventually became the Department of Biomolecular Chemistry, in 1969.<ref name="morgridge1" /> He was promoted to full professor in 1974. He retired from the university in 2005, but still manages a small lab. He and colleague Lloyd smith formed Third Wave Technologies, a company that produced a technology to detect genetic variations. He was on the board of the [[Morgridge Institute for Research]] from 2009 to 2014<ref name="morgridge2">{{cite web|url=https://morgridge.org/story/james-dahlberg-retiring/|title=James Dahlberg retiring from Morgridge Institute|publisher=Morgridge Institute for Research|date=November 12, 2014|accessdate=May 13, 2020}}</ref> and served briefly as interim CEO.<ref name="wsj">{{cite news|url=https://madison.com/wsj/news/local/education/university/morgridge-institute-names-new-ceo/article_e19aa34b-c0a3-5c49-ad9d-b9b792cc7840.html|title=Morgridge Institute names new CEO|last=Simmons|first=Dan|date=January 15, 2013|work=Wisconsin State Journal}}</ref>

*1996 – Elected to the National Academy of Sciences<ref name="NAS">{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/james-e-dahlberg-zdw2xk/|title=James E. Dahlberg|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|access-date=May 13, 2020}}</ref>
